title: 227. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Parameter Conditions for Distinct Real Roots
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+kx+4=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
For a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots, its discriminant must be positive. Here the discriminant is
\[
\Delta=k^2-4(1)(4)=k^2-16
\]
Require \(\Delta>0\), so \(k^2-16>0\). This gives \(k<-4\) or \(k>4\).
questions.hint: Use the condition \(\Delta>0\) for two distinct real roots.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(m\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(m\) does \(x^2-2mx+(m+2)=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
Compute the discriminant, then factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &= (-2m)^2-4(1)(m+2)=4m^2-4m-8=4(m^2-m-2)\\
&= 4(m-2)(m+1)
\end{aligned}
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \((m-2)(m+1)>0\), so \(m<-1\) or \(m>2\).
questions.hint: Factor the discriminant and determine where it is positive.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2+(k-3)x+1=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(k-3)^2-4(1)(1)=(k-3)^2-4
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \((k-3)^2-4>0\), so \((k-3)^2>4\). Thus \(k-3<-2\) or \(k-3>2\), giving \(k<1\) or \(k>5\).

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2-2kx+k^2-k=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(-2k)^2-4(1)(k^2-k)=4k^2-4k^2+4k=4k
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \(4k>0\), so \(k>0\).
questions.hint: Simplify the discriminant before applying the positivity condition.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation with a leading coefficient to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(2x^2-(k+1)x+3=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(k+1)^2-4(2)(3)=(k+1)^2-24
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \((k+1)^2-24>0\), so \((k+1)^2>24\). Thus
\[
k+1<-2\sqrt{6}\quad\text{or}\quad k+1>2\sqrt{6}
\]
which gives \(k<-1-2\sqrt{6}\) or \(k>-1+2\sqrt{6}\).

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(m\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(m\) does \(x^2+(m-1)x+m=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(m-1)^2-4m=m^2-6m+1
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \(m^2-6m+1>0\). The roots of \(m^2-6m+1=0\) are
\[
m=\frac{6\pm\sqrt{36-4}}{2}=3\pm2\sqrt{2}
\]
Since the quadratic opens upward, \(m^2-6m+1>0\) when \(m<3-2\sqrt{2}\) or \(m>3+2\sqrt{2}\).
questions.hint: Find the roots of the discriminant and use the sign of the upward-opening quadratic.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2-(k+2)x+(k+5)=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(k+2)^2-4(k+5)=k^2+4k+4-4k-20=k^2-16
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \(k^2-16>0\). Thus \(k<-4\) or \(k>4\).

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots with a variable leading coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for an equation to be quadratic and have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(kx^2+2x+1=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
For the equation to have two distinct real roots, it must be quadratic, so \(k\ne 0\). The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=2^2-4(k)(1)=4-4k
\]
Require \(\Delta>0\), so \(4-4k>0\), giving \(k<1\). Combining \(k<1\) with \(k\ne 0\), we get \(k<0\) or \(0<k<1\).
questions.hint: Remember that the equation must remain quadratic, so the leading coefficient cannot be zero.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots with a variable leading coefficient
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(m\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots while excluding the degenerate case.
questions.question: For which values of \(m\) does \((m-1)x^2+2(m-1)x+1=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
For the equation to be quadratic, \(m-1\ne 0\), so \(m\ne 1\). Compute the discriminant, then factor:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta &= [2(m-1)]^2-4(m-1)(1)=4(m-1)^2-4(m-1)\\
&= 4(m-1)(m-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(m\ne 1\), require \((m-1)(m-2)>0\). This gives \(m<1\) or \(m>2\).
questions.hint: Factor the discriminant and exclude the value that makes the leading coefficient zero.

questions.concept: Parameter condition for two distinct real roots
questions.learningObjective: Determine the range of \(k\) for a quadratic equation to have two distinct real roots.
questions.question: For which values of \(k\) does \(x^2-2x+k=0\) have two distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is
\[
\Delta=(-2)^2-4(1)(k)=4-4k
\]
For two distinct real roots, require \(4-4k>0\). Thus \(k<1\).
